name: Bobotie
summary: Curry-spiced beef mince with chutney and raisins, baked under a golden egg custard studded with bay leaves.
about: Bobotie has been cooked at the Cape since the 1600s and is closely tied to Cape Malay kitchens; early versions mixed mutton and pork, today it is usually beef. Often called South Africa’s national dish, it is a Sunday-lunch and family-supper favourite, served with yellow rice and chutney.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.note: plus the milk squeezed from the bread

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Soak the bread in the 250 ml milk for 10 minutes while you start the mince.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and fry the onions, stirring now and then, until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, turmeric and coriander and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Turn the heat up to medium-high, add the mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook, stirring, until no pink remains and the juices have mostly cooked away, about 10 minutes.

Squeeze the bread over a jug to keep the milk, then mash the bread into the mince with the chutney, jam, raisins, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Simmer on low for 5 minutes until moist but not wet. Taste and adjust the salt.
Spoon the mince into a greased ovenproof dish of about 30 × 20 cm and press it down into an even layer.
Whisk the eggs with the reserved bread milk and the 125 ml milk. Pour it slowly over the back of a spoon onto the mince so it floats on top, then push the bay leaves into the surface.
Bake uncovered for 35–40 minutes, until the custard is set with no wobble in the centre and golden brown at the edges.
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut into squares. Serve with yellow rice, extra chutney, sliced banana and a tomato-and-onion sambal.
prepNote: Cook the mince up to a day ahead and chill it; add the egg topping just before baking.
